subject: medicine
title: Chronic kidney disease, dialysis and transplantation

steps.tx: Establish chronicity with glomerular filtration rate and albuminuria persisting beyond three months, and map diabetes duration with retinopathy plus resistant **hypertension** headaches. Ask about prolonged painkiller use with blood in urine, deafness or cystic kidneys in the family suggesting **Alport syndrome**, and uraemic itch with nausea, restless legs and hiccups. Note anaemia, gout and bleeding tendency, then stage disease with **filtration and albuminuria bands**.
steps.say: Confirm that reduced filtration or albuminuria has persisted for more than three months before you label the disease chronic. Ask about years of diabetes with eye and foot disease, resistant high pressure with headaches, and prolonged painkiller use with blood in urine. A family history of cystic kidneys or deafness points toward inherited disease. Itching, nausea, restless legs and fatigue complete the uraemic picture before you stage the illness.

steps.tx: Note pale conjunctivae with angular mouth cracks, scratched skin from **uraemic itch** and scratching, and **half and half nails** with brown arcs near the tips. Record periorbital and ankle oedema, listen for a pericardial rub that warns of severe uraemia, and feel every fistula for a **thrill and bruit** before needling. Look for a transplant scar in the groin and test for a stocking pattern neuropathy with restless legs.
steps.say: Inspect the patient for pallor around the eyes and cracks at the angles of the mouth, then look for scratch marks and the pale nails with brown arcs seen in prolonged uraemia. Record swelling around the eyes and ankles and listen carefully for a pericardial rub that warns of advanced disease. Feel the fistula for a buzzing thrill and listen for its bruit, check the groin for a transplant scar, and test sensation in the feet.

steps.tx: The photograph shows a forearm with a tortuous dilated **mature fistula** where the cephalic vein has arterialised for dialysis needling. Labels mark the wrist **anastomosis scar** with its palpable thrill and continuous bruit, plus separate arterial and venous **needling segments** used in rotation. In the exam, always feel the thrill and listen for the bruit, because loss of either signal means the access needs urgent review.
steps.say: Look at the forearm where the surface vein has become tortuous and thick walled after months of arterial flow. The wrist scar marks the surgical join where you should feel a buzzing thrill and hear a continuous machinery murmur. Separate segments higher up the arm are used for the two dialysis needles in rotation. Always check the thrill and bruit at every visit, because sudden loss means the fistula has clotted.

steps.tx: Stage disease with estimated **glomerular filtration rate** and urine albumin to creatinine ratio bands, and track calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone and vitamin D for bone disease. Check iron studies with ferritin and B12 for anaemia, request ultrasound where small echogenic kidneys confirm chronicity, and read the ECG for left ventricular hypertrophy and **hyperkalaemia** change. Separate diabetic, **polycystic and obstructive** patterns before planning access.
steps.say: Stage the disease with the estimated filtration rate and the urine albumin ratio, then follow calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone and vitamin D to protect the bones. Check iron studies and B12 for anaemia, request ultrasound where small bright kidneys confirm chronic damage, and read the ECG for strain and potassium change. Separate diabetic, cystic and obstructive patterns with the history and imaging before you plan dialysis access.

vis.alt: CKD heat map: six GFR stages from G1 at 90 or more to G5 below 15 meet albuminuria bands A1 below 30, A2 30 to 300 and A3 above 300; risk runs low to very high, amber refers and red prepares dialysis.
vis.caption: Two axes, one colour: green monitors, amber refers, red prepares.

steps.tx: Protect residual function with an **angiotensin blocker** for proteinuria and pressure control plus a flozin in diabetes, and correct anaemia with iron and **erythropoietin** support. Bind phosphate with diet and binders with active vitamin D for mineral bone disease, start dialysis through a mature fistula when uraemic indications appear, and work every fit patient up for **transplantation**. Update hepatitis and routine vaccines, restrict potassium, and correct acidosis.
steps.say: Slow decline with blood pressure control using blockers that reduce proteinuria, and add a flozin when diabetes is present. Correct anaemia with iron and hormonal support, control phosphate with diet and binders, and replace active vitamin D for bone health. Create the fistula early so it matures before dialysis begins, assess every suitable patient for transplantation, and keep vaccines current while watching potassium and acid levels.
